html:
A team sport played on ice skates, in which two teams use sticks to drive a rubber puck into the other's goal. Stick and ball games on ice were old, but the first organised indoor game was played in Montreal on 3 March 1875, at the Victoria Skating Rink, using a flat wooden disc instead of a ball.

Students at McGill University wrote some of the first rules soon after. The game spread through Canada, where long, cold winters made outdoor rinks easy. In 1893 the governor general, Lord Stanley, gave a cup for the best amateur team; the Stanley Cup is now the prize of the National Hockey League, founded in 1917.

Hockey became Canada's passion and part of its identity. It spread to the northern United States, Europe and Russia, and became an Olympic sport in 1920. Matches between Canada and the Soviet Union, such as the Summit Series of 1972, became contests of national pride during the Cold War.
